requirements.original: for "(" [ var TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] ValueRef in Expression ")" StatementBlock
requirements.canonical: The range-based loop has the syntax `for` "(" [`var` TypeOrNestedTypeDef] ValueRef `in` Expression ")" StatementBlock.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.4.2 -- for "(" [ var TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] ValueRef in Expression ")" StatementBlock

requirements.original: The range expression is evaluated once before beginning the loop and may be partially initialized.
requirements.canonical: The range expression of a range-based loop IS evaluated exactly once before the loop begins.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.4.2 -- The range expression is evaluated once before beginning the loop and may be partially initialized.

requirements.original: The range expression is evaluated once before beginning the loop and may be partially initialized.
requirements.canonical: The range expression of a range-based loop MAY be partially initialized.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.4.2 -- The range expression is evaluated once before beginning the loop and may be partially initialized.

requirements.original: The range _expression shall evaluate to a value with root type record of, set of, array, octetstring, hexstring, bitstring,_ **charstring or universal charstring.**
requirements.canonical: The range expression of a range-based loop SHALL evaluate to a value whose root type is record of, set of, array, octetstring, hexstring, bitstring, charstring or universal charstring.

ambiguity.issue: The list does not include map types, but NOTE 1 and EXAMPLE 3 iterate over map keys (m.from); chosen reading: map key/value projections count as record of / set of values.
readings: The range expression SHALL be of one of the listed root types, where map key and value projections (`.from`, `.to`) are regarded as set of values.
The range expression SHALL be of one of the listed root types only, so iteration over map keys or values is not allowed.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.4.2 -- The range _expression shall evaluate to a value with root type record of, set of, array, octetstring, hexstring, bitstring,_ **charstring or universal charstring.**

requirements.original: Elements are iterated in sequential order.
requirements.canonical: A range-based loop iterates over the elements of the range expression in sequential order.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.4.2 -- Elements are iterated in sequential order.

requirements.original: In each iteration the appropriate element is assigned to the iteration variable and the statement block is executed.
requirements.canonical: In each iteration of a range-based loop the corresponding element IS assigned to the iteration variable.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.4.2 -- In each iteration the appropriate element is assigned to the iteration variable and the statement block is executed.

requirements.original: In each iteration the appropriate element is assigned to the iteration variable and the statement block is executed.
requirements.canonical: In each iteration of a range-based loop the statement block IS executed after the element has been assigned to the iteration variable.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.4.2 -- In each iteration the appropriate element is assigned to the iteration variable and the statement block is executed.

requirements.original: If the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header, its scope and lifetime is limited to the statement block, i.e. a new iteration variable is initialized in every iteration.
requirements.canonical: If the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header, its scope and lifetime ARE limited to the statement block.
requirements.condition: the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.4.2 -- If the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header, its scope and lifetime is limited to the statement block, i.e. a new iteration variable is initialized in every iteration.

requirements.original: If the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header, its scope and lifetime is limited to the statement block, i.e. a new iteration variable is initialized in every iteration.
requirements.canonical: If the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header, a new iteration variable IS initialized in every iteration.
requirements.condition: the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.4.2 -- If the iteration variable is declared in the for statement header, its scope and lifetime is limited to the statement block, i.e. a new iteration variable is initialized in every iteration.

requirements.original: If the iteration variable is declared outside the for statement, after execution its value will be that of the last iteration.
requirements.canonical: If the iteration variable is declared outside the for statement, its value after the execution of the loop IS that of the last iteration.
requirements.condition: the iteration variable is declared outside the for statement
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.4.2 -- If the iteration variable is declared outside the for statement, after execution its value will be that of the last iteration.

requirements.original: The assignment to the iteration variable follows the rules specified in clause 19.1.1 with the exception that assignment of uninitialized elements is permitted.
requirements.canonical: The assignment of an element to the iteration variable SHALL follow the assignment rules of clause 19.1.1.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.4.2 -- The assignment to the iteration variable follows the rules specified in clause 19.1.1 with the exception that assignment of uninitialized elements is permitted.

requirements.original: The assignment to the iteration variable follows the rules specified in clause 19.1.1 with the exception that assignment of uninitialized elements is permitted.
requirements.canonical: An uninitialized element MAY be assigned to the iteration variable of a range-based loop.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.4.2 -- The assignment to the iteration variable follows the rules specified in clause 19.1.1 with the exception that assignment of uninitialized elements is permitted.

requirements.original: When an uninitialized value is assigned to the iterator variable, the iterator variable becomes uninitialized.
requirements.canonical: When an uninitialized value is assigned to the iteration variable, the iteration variable IS uninitialized.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence uses 'iterator variable' while the rest of the clause uses 'iteration variable'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.4.2 -- When an uninitialized value is assigned to the iterator variable, the iterator variable becomes uninitialized.

requirements.original: A while statement defines a loop that is executed as long as the loop condition holds.
requirements.canonical: A while statement IS a loop that is executed as long as the loop condition holds.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.5 -- A while statement defines a loop that is executed as long as the loop condition holds.

requirements.original: while "(" [(VarInstance|Assignment) ";"] BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock
requirements.canonical: The while statement has the syntax `while` "(" [(VarInstance | Assignment) ";"] BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock.

examples.text: while (v_j<10){ … }

requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.5 -- while "(" [(VarInstance|Assignment) ";"] BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock

requirements.original: The loop condition may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.
requirements.canonical: The loop condition of a while statement MAY be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.5 -- The loop condition may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.

requirements.original: The loop condition may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.
requirements.canonical: The init statement of a while statement IS executed before the loop condition is evaluated.

ambiguity.issue: Unclear whether the init statement executes once before the first evaluation or before every evaluation of the loop condition; chosen reading: once.
readings: The init statement of a while statement IS executed once, before the loop condition is evaluated for the first time.
The init statement of a while statement IS executed before each evaluation of the loop condition.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.5 -- The loop condition may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.

requirements.original: The scope of variables declared within an init statement shall be limited to the while statement.
requirements.canonical: The scope of a variable declared within the init statement of a while statement SHALL be limited to the while statement.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.5 -- The scope of variables declared within an init statement shall be limited to the while statement.

requirements.original: The loop condition shall be checked at the beginning of each new loop iteration.
requirements.canonical: The loop condition of a while statement SHALL be checked at the beginning of each new loop iteration.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.5 -- The loop condition shall be checked at the beginning of each new loop iteration.

requirements.original: If the loop condition does not hold, then the loop is exited and execution shall continue with the statement, which immediately follows the while loop.
requirements.canonical: If the loop condition of a while statement does not hold, the loop SHALL be exited and execution SHALL continue with the statement immediately following the while loop.
requirements.condition: the loop condition does not hold
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.5 -- If the loop condition does not hold, then the loop is exited and execution shall continue with the statement, which immediately follows the while loop.

requirements.original: If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt, alststep or interleave, then the loop is terminated, too.
requirements.canonical: If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt statement, altstep or interleave statement, the while loop IS terminated.
requirements.condition: the break statement is not within an enclosed loop, alt, altstep or interleave

ambiguity.issue: The text uses the misspelling 'alststep' instead of 'altstep'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.5 -- If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt, alststep or interleave, then the loop is terminated, too.

requirements.original: A do-while statement defines a loop that is executed up until the loop condition does not hold.
requirements.canonical: A do-while statement IS a loop that is executed until the loop condition does not hold.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.6 -- A do-while statement defines a loop that is executed up until the loop condition does not hold.

requirements.original: do StatementBlock while "(" BooleanExpression ")"
requirements.canonical: The do-while statement has the syntax `do` StatementBlock `while` "(" BooleanExpression ")".

examples.text: do { … } while (v_j<10);

requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.6 -- do StatementBlock while "(" BooleanExpression ")"

requirements.original: The do-while loop is identical to a while loop with the exception that the loop condition shall be checked at the end of each loop iteration.
requirements.canonical: A do-while loop IS identical to a while loop except for the point at which the loop condition is checked.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.6 -- The do-while loop is identical to a while loop with the exception that the loop condition shall be checked at the end of each loop iteration.

requirements.original: The do-while loop is identical to a while loop with the exception that the loop condition shall be checked at the end of each loop iteration.
requirements.canonical: The loop condition of a do-while statement SHALL be checked at the end of each loop iteration.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.6 -- The do-while loop is identical to a while loop with the exception that the loop condition shall be checked at the end of each loop iteration.

requirements.original: This means when using a do-while loop the behaviour is executed at least once before the loop condition is evaluated for the first time.
requirements.canonical: The statement block of a do-while loop IS executed at least once before the loop condition is evaluated for the first time.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.6 -- This means when using a do-while loop the behaviour is executed at least once before the loop condition is evaluated for the first time.

requirements.original: If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt, alststep or interleave, then the loop is terminated, too.
requirements.canonical: If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt statement, altstep or interleave statement, the do-while loop IS terminated.
requirements.condition: the break statement is not within an enclosed loop, alt, altstep or interleave

ambiguity.issue: The text uses the misspelling 'alststep' instead of 'altstep'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.6 -- If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt, alststep or interleave, then the loop is terminated, too.

requirements.original: The label statement allows the specification of labels in test cases, functions and altsteps.
requirements.canonical: A label statement MAY be used in test cases, functions and altsteps.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.7 -- The label statement allows the specification of labels in test cases, functions and altsteps.

requirements.original: label LabelIdentifier
requirements.canonical: The label statement has the syntax `label` LabelIdentifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.7 -- label LabelIdentifier

requirements.original: The label is used by the goto statement (see clause 19.8) to transfer control to a labelled statement.
requirements.canonical: A label IS used by the goto statement to transfer control to the labelled statement.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.7 -- The label is used by the goto statement (see clause 19.8) to transfer control to a labelled statement.

requirements.original: a) A label statement can be used freely like other TTCN-3 behavioural program statements according to the syntax rules defined in annex A.
requirements.canonical: A label statement MAY be used like any other TTCN-3 behavioural program statement according to the syntax rules of annex A.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.7 -- a) A label statement can be used freely like other TTCN-3 behavioural program statements according to the syntax rules defined in annex A.

requirements.original: It can be used before or after a TTCN-3 statement
requirements.canonical: A label statement MAY be placed before or after a TTCN-3 statement.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.7 -- It can be used before or after a TTCN-3 statement

requirements.original: but not as the first statement of an alternative or top alternative in an alt statement, interleave statement or altstep.
requirements.canonical: A label statement SHALL NOT be the first statement of an alternative or top alternative in an alt statement, interleave statement or altstep.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.7 -- but not as the first statement of an alternative or top alternative in an alt statement, interleave statement or altstep.

requirements.original: b) Labels used following the label keyword shall be unique among all labels defined in the same test case, function or altstep.
requirements.canonical: A label defined by a label statement SHALL be unique among all labels defined in the same test case, function or altstep.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.7 -- b) Labels used following the label keyword shall be unique among all labels defined in the same test case, function or altstep.

requirements.original: A goto statement performs a jump to a label.
requirements.canonical: A goto statement performs a jump to a label.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.8 -- A goto statement performs a jump to a label.

requirements.original: goto LabelIdentifier
requirements.canonical: The goto statement has the syntax `goto` LabelIdentifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.8 -- goto LabelIdentifier

requirements.original: The goto statement can be used in functions, test cases and altsteps to transfer control to a labelled statement.
requirements.canonical: A goto statement MAY be used in functions, test cases and altsteps to transfer control to a labelled statement.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.8 -- The goto statement can be used in functions, test cases and altsteps to transfer control to a labelled statement.

requirements.original: The goto statement provides the possibility to jump freely, i.e. forwards and backwards, within a sequence of statements, to jump out of a single compound statement (e.g. a while loop) and to jump over several levels out of nested compound statements (e.g. nested alternatives).
requirements.canonical: A goto statement MAY jump forwards and backwards within a sequence of statements.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.8 -- The goto statement provides the possibility to jump freely, i.e. forwards and backwards, within a sequence of statements, to jump out of a single compound statement (e.g. a while loop) and to jump over several levels out of nested compound statements (e.g. nested alternatives).

requirements.original: The goto statement provides the possibility to jump freely, i.e. forwards and backwards, within a sequence of statements, to jump out of a single compound statement (e.g. a while loop) and to jump over several levels out of nested compound statements (e.g. nested alternatives).
requirements.canonical: A goto statement MAY jump out of a single compound statement.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.8 -- The goto statement provides the possibility to jump freely, i.e. forwards and backwards, within a sequence of statements, to jump out of a single compound statement (e.g. a while loop) and to jump over several levels out of nested compound statements (e.g. nested alternatives).

requirements.original: The goto statement provides the possibility to jump freely, i.e. forwards and backwards, within a sequence of statements, to jump out of a single compound statement (e.g. a while loop) and to jump over several levels out of nested compound statements (e.g. nested alternatives).
requirements.canonical: A goto statement MAY jump over several levels out of nested compound statements.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.8 -- The goto statement provides the possibility to jump freely, i.e. forwards and backwards, within a sequence of statements, to jump out of a single compound statement (e.g. a while loop) and to jump over several levels out of nested compound statements (e.g. nested alternatives).

requirements.original: a) It is not allowed to jump out of or into functions, test cases and altsteps.
requirements.canonical: A goto statement SHALL NOT jump out of a function, test case or altstep.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.8 -- a) It is not allowed to jump out of or into functions, test cases and altsteps.

requirements.original: a) It is not allowed to jump out of or into functions, test cases and altsteps.
requirements.canonical: A goto statement SHALL NOT jump into a function, test case or altstep.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.8 -- a) It is not allowed to jump out of or into functions, test cases and altsteps.

requirements.original: b) It is not allowed to jump into a sequence of statements defined in a compound statement (i.e. alt statement, while loop, for loop, if-else statement, do-while loop and the interleave statement).
requirements.canonical: A goto statement SHALL NOT jump into a sequence of statements defined in a compound statement (alt statement, while loop, for loop, if-else statement, do-while loop or interleave statement).

ambiguity.issue: The list introduced by 'i.e.' omits select case and select union statements and plain statement blocks; chosen reading: the list is exhaustive.
readings: A goto statement SHALL NOT jump into the statements of an alt, while, for, if-else, do-while or interleave statement only.
A goto statement SHALL NOT jump into any compound statement, including select case and select union statements.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.8 -- b) It is not allowed to jump into a sequence of statements defined in a compound statement (i.e. alt statement, while loop, for loop, if-else statement, do-while loop and the interleave statement).

requirements.original: c) It is not allowed to use the goto statement within an interleave statement.
requirements.canonical: A goto statement SHALL NOT be used within an interleave statement.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 19.8 -- c) It is not allowed to use the goto statement within an interleave statement.
